His great-grandfather Li had served as Grand Master of Admonition to the heir apparent; after death he was posthumously honored as Minister of Rites.

In the tenth month he was appointed acting Left Regular Attendant of the Scattered Riders, concurrently Censor-in-Chief, military commissioner of Youzhou and Lulong, chief administrator of Youzhou, and concurrently Grand Censor.

In the tenth month he was appointed acting Left Regular Attendant of the Scattered Riders, concurrently Vice Censor-in-Chief, military commissioner of Youzhou and Lulong, chief administrator of Youzhou, and concurrently Censor-in-Chief.
御史中丞 is Vice Censor-in-Chief. 御史大夫 rendering.
That same year Zhu Ci memorialized the throne, asking that his younger brother Tao lead twenty-five hundred troops to the western capital for autumn defense.

京西 means west of the capital.
After Jingzhou was pacified, Zhu Ci was made Grand Secretariat Director and returned to garrison Fengxiang, while Prince Shu Li Rang was given nominal command of Jingyuan.
After Jingzhou was pacified, Zhu Ci was made Director of the Secretariat and returned to garrison Fengxiang, while Prince Shu Li Rang was given nominal command of Jingyuan.
In the second year Zhu Ci was made Grand Preceptor.
In the second year Zhu Ci was made Grand Commandant.

In the fourth month of the third year Zhang Yi replaced Zhu Ci as acting military commissioner of Fengxiang and Longyou. Zhu Ci was kept at the capital, his substantive fief was raised to one thousand households, and one of his sons was given a regular official post; his titles as military commissioner of Youzhou and Lulong, Grand Preceptor, and Grand Secretariat Director remained unchanged.

Among Zheng Tian's officers was the junior commander Dou Mei, a warrior without peer: every night he led a hundred volunteers deep into the capital, torched the gate towers, beheaded the enemy, and withdrew before dawn, leaving the rebels shaken with fear.
